$comment: Committed PLZG flow snapshot. Clause (b) of the delivery gate (scripts/validate_delivery_coordinates.py) requires this file to be FRESH -- as_of inside the sprint window it declares, and that sprint not yet ended -- and HONEST, with work_item_age naming exactly counts.wip items. wip MAY BE 0: the previous wip > 0 rule was removed by owner ruling 2026-08-02 (PLZG-130) because it tested snapshot timing rather than health, and rewarded a fake transition. Shape matches the pm-skills jira_snapshot_bridge.py '--to flow' output so the two are interchangeable. THIS IS A SNAPSHOT, NOT A LIVE READING: it is true as of the as_of timestamp and nowhere else. Re-query Jira before citing any number here -- the board owns these facts, this file does not.
source: Atlassian MCP searchJiraIssuesUsingJql against tasteslikegood.atlassian.net, cloudId 029decc8-e09a-4d55-92f8-20d9ca64ca13
regenerate: project = PLZG (total) / statusCategory = Done (done) / statusCategory = "In Progress" (wip), then recompute work_item_age from each WIP item's created date

work_item_age.summary: validate_delivery_coordinates.py clause (b) passes green on a frozen snapshot

sprint.name: PLZG Sprint 3
sprint.goal: Every governed document declares which of its claims about state are proven and by what, and the tier ladder gains a home for delivery policy.

at_sprint_start.note: WIP was 0 and work_item_age empty because the board used only 'To Do' and 'Done' -- nobody used the In Progress transition, which already existed (status id 3, transition id 21). The fix was behavioural, not structural; no Jira admin change was required.

forecast_blackout.reason: Sample is large enough (56 completions) but non-stationary: an 11-week zero-throughput gap sits inside it, so Monte Carlo cannot distinguish 'team paused' from 'team is slow' and silently prices dormancy into every forecast. See specs/sprint-2-charter.md section 3.
forecast_blackout.lift_condition: 10+ completions carrying real started->resolved timestamps, drawn from a window containing no zero-throughput weeks.
